questions.subject: FILM_STUDIES
questions.learningObjective: Define and distinguish key film studies concepts
questions.stem: Which statement best defines Mise-en-scène?

options.text: It is the arrangement of everything that appears in the frame, including setting, actors, lighting, and composition.
It is the precise movement and positioning of actors within a scene as planned by the director.
It is the arrangement of visual elements within the frame to guide the eye and create meaning.
It is the physical location and environment in which a scene takes place, whether real or built.

questions.explanation: It is the arrangement of everything that appears in the frame, including setting, actors, lighting, and composition. This is precisely what Mise-en-scène means; the alternatives describe Blocking, Composition, Setting, which are different ideas.
questions.hint: Recall the specific meaning of Mise-en-scène.

options.text: It is the physical location and environment in which a scene takes place, whether real or built.
It is the arrangement of everything that appears in the frame, including setting, actors, lighting, and composition.
It is the precise movement and positioning of actors within a scene as planned by the director.
It is the deliberate use of light and shadow to shape mood, focus attention, and model form.

questions.explanation: It is the physical location and environment in which a scene takes place, whether real or built. This is precisely what Setting means; the alternatives describe Mise-en-scène, Blocking, Lighting design, which are different ideas.
questions.hint: Recall the specific meaning of Setting.
